_sample_data: EVERY value below is ILLUSTRATIVE — the scope names, owners, use cases and statuses describe no real deployment, team or engagement. Owners use @example.com (RFC 2606) so they cannot be mistaken for people: an invented but realistic name is indistinguishable from a real one to a reader, a search engine, and whoever happens to share it. Enforced by ai-standards/scripts/check_example_names.py. Replace all of it with your own.
_comment: Configurable context-scope registry. Levels are YOURS to define — rename, add, or remove them (consulting: enterprise>tenant>engagement; corp: enterprise>department>team>personal). The scope tree maps 1:1 to directories under workspace/<workspaceRoot>/, so an agent run 'at' a node sees that node's dir plus every ancestor's (Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md upward) — inheritance is structural. Siblings are invisible. The router enforces everything else in this file.

levelDefaults._comment: Controls applied to every node of a level unless the node overrides. pii: off|warn|block (outbound prompt guard). isolation: pool (shared runner, cwd-scoped) | silo (dedicated runner required). promotion: review = content moves UP a level only after scrub+generalize+human review. identityGroup: who may invoke this scope (maps to a Google Group). retentionDays: null = keep. allowedTools (optional, per-node): array of Claude Code tool names (e.g. ["Read","Grep","Edit","Bash"]) the router passes to the runner as --allowedTools; UNLISTED tools are effectively denied — defence-in-depth on top of the firewall/mounts. Omit to allow the runner's defaults. See GUARDRAILS.md.

conflicts._comment: Ethical walls. Listed pairs must NEVER share a pooled runner — the router refuses pool dispatch for them (silo + runnerHost required).
